articles.title: Calls for Immediate Deportation of Grooming Gang Offenders
articles.excerpt: A recent article highlights the need for the immediate deportation of grooming gang offenders, referencing scandals in Rochdale and other towns.
articles.content_html:
A recent article has sparked discussions about the immediate deportation of grooming gang offenders. The piece references the grooming gang scandals in Rotherham, Rochdale, Telford, and other locations, which exposed the organised abuse of mainly white working-class girls by groups often of Pakistani heritage.

The article argues that offenders should face immediate deportation as part of a broader response to these scandals. It highlights the serious nature of the crimes and the impact on the victims and their families.

This call for action has generated a range of opinions, with some supporting the need for stricter measures against offenders, while others raise concerns about the implications of such policies.

The discussion continues to evolve as community members and leaders consider the best ways to address the issues raised by these scandals.

articles.title: Minor Delays on Rochdale Line Due to Vehicle Fault
articles.excerpt: A vehicle fault is causing minor delays on the Rochdale line, with additional service updates affecting other Metrolink stops.
articles.content_html:
A vehicle fault is causing minor delays on the Rochdale line, according to Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM). The delays are expected to continue until further notice.

In addition, essential improvement works will take place at Prestwich Metrolink stop from 12:00am on 18 May until 11:59pm on 19 August. Tram services will not be affected, but there may be an increased presence of staff at this stop during this period.

TfGM has also reported that the escalator to exit Piccadilly Metrolink stop to the city centre or mainline station is currently out of service. Passengers are advised to follow the signage for the lift from platform level to the mezzanine and mainline station.

Furthermore, the escalator at Manchester Airport is out of service. Customers requiring step-free access should contact the Metrolink contact centre for additional journey planning support or use the customer service help point on-stop. The contact number is 0161 244 1000, with lines open from 7am to 8pm Monday to Friday and 8am to 8pm on weekends and Bank Holidays.

articles.title: Plans for Demolition of Flats in Lower Falinge Resurface
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has revealed new plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, sparking distress among remaining residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, which contain 126 homes, as part of a redevelopment project. The proposal aims to replace the existing buildings with 270 new homes, including a mix of flats and houses, on land between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street.

The blocks targeted for demolition include Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, and Vaynor. Only the Zedburgh block, which is still occupied, remains. Andy Roche, a resident of the Zedburgh block since 1988, expressed his distress over the plans, stating that he and his partner are both autistic and the prospect of eviction is affecting their health.

RBH previously halted demolition plans last year following a successful legal challenge from campaigners. Residents were informed that RBH needed to demonstrate a clear vision for the land rather than leaving it vacant. Despite the new plans, Roche feels that the concerns of residents have not been adequately addressed, saying, "I don't believe they have listened to the residents of the estate at all."

The estate has seen significant changes over the years, with previous demolition work leading to the construction of 100 new homes. However, the remaining blocks have been described as no longer fit for purpose, with RBH stating that they have exceeded their lifespan. The area has faced challenges, including being labelled a 'sink estate' by former Prime Minister David Cameron in 2016, which has contributed to its current state.

articles.title: Rochdale Council to Host Annual Sensory Awareness Day
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council will hold its annual sensory awareness day at Number One Riverside on 13 August, providing information and advice on sensory issues.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council will host its annual sensory awareness day at Number One Riverside on Thursday, 13 August, from 10am to 3pm.

The event aims to provide a range of information and advice on sensory issues, catering to those who may benefit from support in this area.

Attendees will have the opportunity to access resources and speak with professionals about sensory challenges and solutions.

The council encourages anyone interested to attend and take advantage of the free services available during the event.

articles.title: Lift at Derker Tram Stop Out of Service Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers travelling towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
A lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 10:16am on Monday, 10 August 2026, and will remain unavailable until further notice.

Passengers travelling towards Manchester can access the Manchester-bound platform via a ramp from Cromford Street. Those travelling away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street and must cross the tracks to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and advises customers to plan their journeys accordingly.

Further information will be provided as it becomes available.
